original_card.first_experiment: First check whether the scatter repair has been adopted. If still open, independently reproduce #2977 symbolic-versus-exported parity on the tiny duplicate fixture, compare the selected unique-row positive control, and define either enforced uniqueness or consistent multiplicity semantics. A bounded guard-adoption patch must preserve valid inputs and test the actual exported action. Stop after this obligation; no full historical replay or frontier change follows from the mutant alone.

actual_scope: Answer #3696 open question 2 on the pinned tuned word: are the four named B[0] checker rejects exhaustive for dest-in-sources Sym/Exp divergence? Prove a dest-in closed form, enumerate all length-≤2 source lists at destination 111 over n=661 registers, and show exactly 661 divergences of which only two lie among the four named rejects.
scope_change_reason: Authorized follow-up to #3696 OQ2 under the supplier-boundary cascade. Dest-free Sym/Exp agreement is already published and is not restated as the claim; the new obligation is exhaustiveness of the four rejects versus the complete length-≤2 divergence set, plus the dest-in closed form that makes the census checkable.
bottleneck_link: Knowing that reject samples are not a divergence taxonomy prevents treating four mutants as a complete gate-operand contract.
stop_rule: Stop after the closed form, length-≤2 census, named-reject comparison, checker spot controls, and certificate admission. No dest-absent schema corollary, exporter rewrite, native replay, or kappa change.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json, PROOF.md, verify.py, independent.py and test_package.py. Closed form matches linear Sym/Exp on n≤8,len≤5 and on all length-≤2 lists at d=111; exactly 661 divergences; named diverge count 2; four_exhaustive=false; checker rejects the four named mutants and four spot divergences.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for reading the #3696 cascade, deriving the dest-in closed form, implementing the length-≤2 census and package controls, and writing this package.
